questions.question: Which is the deepest known point in the Earth's oceans?
questions.hint: Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench reaches about 11,000 meters below sea level, making it the deepest known point on Earth.

questions.question: Which tree is known as the 'Tree of Life' in arid regions due to its survival ability?
questions.hint: The Baobab can store thousands of liters of water, helping it survive extreme drought conditions.

questions.question: In 'Breaking Bad,' what is Walter White's alias in the drug world?
questions.hint: Walter White adopts the alias 'Heisenberg' as his criminal identity in the series Breaking Bad.

questions.question: Which series features the fictional continent 'Westeros'?
questions.hint: Westeros is one of the main continents in the world created by George R. R. Martin.

questions.question: What is the term for a system where citizens vote to elect their leaders?
questions.hint: In a democracy, power is held by the people through voting and representation.

questions.question: Which document is considered the foundation of modern human rights law?
questions.hint: Adopted in 1948 by the United Nations, it outlines fundamental human rights for all people.

questions.question: Which empire was ruled by Genghis Khan?
questions.hint: Genghis Khan founded the Mongol Empire, one of the largest empires in history.

questions.question: Which war lasted from 1914 to 1918?
questions.hint: World War I was a global conflict triggered by tensions between major European powers.

questions.question: Which country has won the most FIFA World Cup titles?
questions.hint: Brazil has won the FIFA World Cup 5 times, more than any other nation.

questions.question: In tennis, what is the term for a score of 40–40?
questions.hint: Deuce occurs when both players have 40 points, requiring a two-point lead to win.

questions.question: Which river is the longest in the world (commonly accepted)?
questions.hint: The Nile stretches over 6,600 km and is widely recognized as the longest river.

questions.question: Which country has the most natural lakes?
questions.hint: Canada has more lakes than the rest of the world combined.

questions.question: What particle gives atoms their identity?
questions.hint: The number of protons determines the atomic number and element type.

questions.question: What is the speed of light in vacuum approximately?
questions.hint: Light travels at about 299,792 km/s in a vacuum, commonly rounded to 300,000 km/s.

questions.question: Which country is famous for the martial art 'Karate'?
questions.hint: Karate originated in Okinawa, Japan, and became globally popular.

questions.question: Which festival marks the end of Ramadan?
questions.hint: Eid-ul-Fitr is celebrated after completing the month of fasting (Ramadan).

questions.question: Which gas makes up most of Earth's atmosphere?
questions.hint: About 78% of Earth's atmosphere is nitrogen gas.

questions.question: Which is the smallest independent country in the world?
questions.hint: Vatican City covers only about 0.49 km² and is the spiritual center of the Catholic Church.

questions.question: What is the main gas responsible for global warming?
questions.hint: CO₂ traps heat in the atmosphere and contributes significantly to climate change.

questions.question: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.hint: Neil Armstrong stepped onto the Moon during Apollo 11 in 1969.
